newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: AUSTRALIA STOCKS END 1.6 PCT DOWN ON U.S. FALL.
newsitem.headline: AUSTRALIA STOCKS END 1.6 PCT DOWN ON U.S. FALL.

text.p: 10yrbond futs 93.190 -0.230 Gold NY 327.15 Asia 327.00
AUD US$0.7360 (Fri US$0.7311) CRB Index cl 243.69 +0.86
*Stocks end near day's low on U.S. plunge Friday, despite a full recovery by BHP. Volume 286.92 million, A$793.85 million value, 1,117 stocks traded, 282 steady, 235 up, 600 down.
The Australian share market closed sharply lower on Monday in response to a slump in the local bond market and a plunge on Wall Street last Friday.
A recovery in the market fortunes of bellwether stock BHP failed to inspire a more widespread upturn.
"Nothing could turn the trend today," one dealer said.
The All Ordinaries index closed 44.2 points down at 2,667.2, representing a fall of 1.6 percent.
September share price index futures came sank 72 points to 2,655, its lowest level since July 16 and a 12.2 point discount to the underlying index.

BHP, which accounts for about eight percent of the total market, slumped 28.5 cents in early trade to a four month low in continued reaction to Friday's news of management turmoil at the petroleum, minerals and steel giant. It recovered to a high of A$17.16 before falling back to end two cents up at A$17.01.
"A management crisis on top of galloping costs is not good, but it had already fallen a lot," one Sydney-based dealer said, adding investors needed more time to evaluate BHP's situation.
"Once (BHP) has ironed out those managerial problems they should be pretty much alright," said Mark Pervan of Daiwa Securities in Melbourne.
Rio Tinto gained ground in early trade, but it fell back as BHP recovered and closed three cents lower at A$21.27. Some dealers said investors had switched from BHP to Rio Tinto in morning trade.
"It performed particularly well at the expense of BHP. Rio will probably come off a bit more as BHP recovers," Pervan said.
Miner WMC fell in line with the market, down 10 cents to A$7.39, ahead of Wednesday's full-year report.
Analysts polled by Reuters expect a 44 percent plunge in net profit to A$217.5 million, mainly as a result of last year's weak metal prices.
The number of declines far outnumbered advances. None of the blue chips were among the top net gainers as the added pressure of a sharply weaker local bond market took its toll on market sentiment.

An initial mark up in Australian bond yields after Friday's massive sell-off in U.S. Treasuries turned more aggressive in afternoon trading as U.S. hedge funds sold futures heavily. The 10-year bond yield rose 22 basis points to 6.83 percent.
"The banks and other interest rate sensitive stocks are getting hit pretty hard," one dealer said.
National Australia Bank fell 34 cents to A$19.29.

Traders seemed to take little notice of comments by managing director Don Argus who said NAB's lending margins were stabilising and that margins results for the fourth quarter will not disappoint the market.

Commonwealth Bank lost 17 cents to A$16.65 ahead of Wednesday's full-year report. Tight lending margins would have hurt profits in the second half, but the bank is set to reveal plans for a special dividend or a share buyback, analysts said.
News Corp ended 15 cents down at A$5.92, partly due to arbitrage related to the US$1.35 billion stock-and-debt deal to acquire Heritage Media Corp, dealers said.

One of the day's weakest stocks was transport group Brambles with an 81 cent dip to A$27.59. "It's been going up so strongly recently that the fall is no real surprise," said Andrew Sekely, head of equities at Intersuisse Ltd in Sydney.
Lend Lease was another where profit-taking added to the decline. The property and financial services group fell 63.5 cents to A$29.415 ahead of the full-year report on Thursday.
Analysts expect a 13 percent rise in pre-abnormal profit to A$317.7 million.
The gold sector slowly gave in to the wider decline but still ended 0.4 percent up on the back of higher bullion prices.
Resolute was one of the strongest gold stocks, closing seven cents higher at A$1.85, while index heavyweight Normandy Mining rose one cent to A$1.53.
At 5.20 p.m. (0720 GMT), the Australian dollar held on to its earlier gains to trade at US$0.7368/73, up from US$0.7312/17 on Friday, but currency traders said it remained vulnerable.
